items.title: llm-echo 0.5
items.summary: The llm-echo debug plugin's simulated token usage counts now account for tool calls, system prompts, and reasoning tokens in a new release.

items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
items.summary: Anthropic has granted external evaluators employee-like access to assess its models' risks, with METR embedding a team in its office.

items.title: AI agents chasing a $465 train refund invented excuses, leaked medical data, and spammed an MP's office
items.summary: Researcher Matilda Glynn-Henley warns of "agentic flooding" if autonomous AI assistants are deployed at scale, potentially overwhelming agencies and businesses. The study has limits and does not support a reliable ranking of the six models, the article says.

items.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
items.summary: MIT researchers created a multimodal AI model combining 3D atomic structures with natural language descriptions to better identify materials.

items.title: OnlyFans Creators Are Pissed That Meta Lets Muse Talk Dirty
items.summary: OnlyFans creators criticized Meta for allowing its Muse AI agent to sext adults while their Instagram accounts face restrictions.

items.title: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft without any human help
items.summary: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents autonomously beat Minecraft, slaying the Ender Dragon without human input, according to the report. The agents organized themselves without assigned roles, over 27 hours and 14 minutes, at a stated cost of $1,620.

items.title: No agenda, no rush, no leaving San Francisco: Benchmark’s partners on investing in a frenzied market
items.summary: Benchmark partners said they invest at their usual pace of two or three new bets per year per partner despite a faster market. Peter Fenton said Benchmark's core fund was held at $500 million for 20 years and has now been adjusted for inflation.

items.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
items.summary: Anthropic announced a public benefit fund committing 5% of its shares, with an option to add 2% for every 50% value increase.

items.title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce
items.summary: Disney agreed to make employment offers to at least 60 Character.AI employees, the majority of the workforce, with estimated $60 million in annual compensation, per a legal filing. The filing says the "vast majority" of Character.AI employees offered jobs at Disney accepted them, though it is a stalking horse bid so another company could offer more.

items.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Rivian’s next act
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe wants the company to be much more than an EV maker. Rivian has a $5.8 billion joint technology venture with VW Group focused on electric architecture and software. Scaringe discussed expanding the VW joint venture to cover AI and autonomy and licensing Rivian’s tech to many different brands.

items.title: Anthropic has nearly stopped hiring junior staff because AI agents now work six times as many hours
items.summary: Anthropic reports its AI agents logged six times as many work hours as human employees by August 2026, and it cites growing agent capability as the reason for fewer junior technical hires.

items.title: Cities want to put the boot on robotaxis
items.summary: The article reports that, with federal rules stalled, cities and states are creating their own regulations for autonomous vehicles.

items.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
items.summary: Two German courts have held Google liable for its AI-generated search summaries as the company's own statements. The Aachen Regional Court barred Google from spreading false claims about a doctor, a decision not yet final.

items.title: Anthropic consults law firms to set fair negotiation norms before AI agents start cutting deals
items.summary: Anthropic is consulting law firms to develop fair negotiation norms for AI agents that could haggle over prices, resolve complaints, or improve contract offers, according to the Financial Times. Anthropic has shown in experiments that stronger models negotiate better deals, which could widen societal inequality.
